$comment: Single source of truth for which taw-theme paths are framework-owned and safe to sync into a client project. Read by both the update-theme Claude Code skill and TAW\CLI\SyncCommand (php bin/taw sync) — keep them pointed at this file rather than hardcoding the lists twice. Tier 1 is always overwritten without confirmation; Tier 2 is diffed and requires human review before being applied; anything not listed is never read or touched.

tier1.$comment: keep_edited: the sha256 of every version the taw-theme scaffold shipped (its git history). Sync replaces the site's copy only when it is one of these (an unedited copy) or missing; a copy the site edited (helpers of its own) is kept and reported, never overwritten. Add the new hash when the scaffold's copy changes (SyncCommandTest fails until you do).

skillsReconcile.$comment: How `type: skills-dir` entries are synced. Claude Code and the agents runtime only auto-discover skills in `.claude/skills/` and `.agents/skills/`, so framework-managed and site-authored skills have to share the same directory — a plain `rsync -a --delete` (what `type: dir` does) would destroy any skill the client authored for itself. Instead the sync reconciles per skill subdirectory: every skill present in the canonical taw-theme repo is overwritten in place (fresh canonical copy, every run), except when the client's copy of that name says `owner: site` — then it is kept and reported as a `clash` (the framework copy is not installed until the site renames or removes its own); a skill subdirectory present in the client but NOT in canonical is resolved by reading the `owner:` key in its SKILL.md YAML frontmatter — `owner: taw` means it is a framework skill that has been retired upstream, so it is DELETED; `owner: site` means the client authored it, so it is PRESERVED untouched and reported; no `owner:` key (or an unreadable SKILL.md) is treated as unknown — PRESERVED but reported with a warning so a human can decide. Every canonical framework skill carries `owner: taw` in its frontmatter, which is also what makes framework vs site skills greppable in a client's tree (`grep -rl 'owner: taw' .claude/skills`).

manifestMerge.$comment: How sync compares the structured Tier 2 manifests (TAW\CLI\ManifestMerge). Only the listed sections are read; within them, keys and repositories the scaffold has and the site lacks are suggested (add), a dependency whose scaffold constraint has a higher lower bound is suggested (bump), and any other difference goes to review. Keys only the site has are its own (emailit, photoswipe, taw/hub-companion…) and are always kept: nothing is ever removed. Optional features are lines new sites get from the scaffold but existing sites only take on purpose; they are reported as optional, never suggested. Labels are dot paths, or repositories[<url>]. `php bin/taw sync --apply-manifests` writes add + bump.

$never: tests/Unit/ is deliberately never listed here, in either tier, and must never become a 'dir' entry — it holds each client project's own block tests (tests/Unit/Blocks/{Name}Test.php), content this manifest doesn't own. A 'dir' entry syncs via 'rsync -a --delete', which would silently delete every client-authored test not present in the canonical repo. Only the harness itself (tests/bootstrap.php, tests/TestCase.php, phpunit.xml) is framework-owned; individual test files are not. The same hazard for .claude/skills/ and .agents/skills/ (client sites legitimately author their own skills) is handled by 'type: skills-dir' + the skillsReconcile rules above, not by omitting them.

agentDocs.$comment: Since v1.91.0 the agent docs (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .github/copilot-instructions.md, .windsurfrules) are no longer Tier 2. The framework's part ships with taw/core in resources/agents/<classic|block>/ and updates with it; a theme keeps short site-owned files that import (CLAUDE.md) or point to (the others) it, marked `taw:agent-doc`. `sync --apply` (when taw.json's update.docs allows) and `bin/taw docs:sync --apply` replace old full copies with those files (TAW\Update\AgentDocs). README.md is the site's own: never synced.

configFiles.$comment: Since v1.91.0 vite.config.js and phpstan.neon are no longer Tier 2: their base ships with taw/core (classicTheme() in resources/vite/taw-vite.mjs, resources/phpstan/classic.neon) and the theme keeps a short `taw:config` file of its own. `sync --apply` (when taw.json's update.scaffold allows) and `bin/taw configs:sync --apply` replace only unedited copies (resources/configs/known.json); edited ones are reported with the by-hand steps (TAW\Update\ConfigFiles). phpunit.xml is the site's own: never synced.
